_comment: Frozen benchmark tasks. expected_files is the number of source files a competent build needs; it is the denominator for the files-touched metric, not a rule the agent is told about.

easy.task: Build a single-page site that shows the current UTC time, updating every second. It needs a heading that reads 'UTC Clock', the live time in an element with id="clock", and a button with id="freeze" that stops and restarts the updating. Plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file. No frameworks, no build step.

medium.task: Build a tip calculator site. It needs an input with id="bill" for the bill amount, an input with id="tip-percent" for the tip percentage defaulting to 18, a control with id="split" for splitting between 1 to 12 people, and three outputs with ids "tip-amount", "total" and "per-person" that update as the inputs change. Handle an empty or non-numeric bill without showing NaN. Keep it to static files.

hard.task: Build a markdown note-taking site that persists to localStorage. It needs a list of notes with id="note-list", a button with id="new-note" that creates one, a textarea with id="editor", a live rendered preview in an element with id="preview" supporting headings, bold, italic, links, inline code and unordered lists, and a search box with id="search" that filters the note list by title and body. Notes must survive a page reload. Write the markdown renderer yourself; no markdown library.
